A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LA-CDM and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be matched across the revised methods, experiments, and document structure.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIMIC-CDM experiments, including diagnostic performance, calibration, a hypothesis-agent ablation, backbone comparisons, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original diagnostic and calibration results, hypothesis-agent and cost-reward ablations, pricing-sensitivity experiments, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 replace PPO with GRPO for both reinforcement-learning objectives and add a cumulative test-cost penalty to action-selection training. The shared-weight, two-agent architecture, supervised hypothesis training, and logarithmic calibration reward remain.

E1.justification: Clinical coverage remains the same four-condition MIMIC-CDM dataset and available diagnostic tests. Appendix D adds simulated pricing scenarios: small institutional price variations and an extreme complete-blood-count penalty. These extend economic environment coverage without adding actual hospitals or patient populations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator methods: OASST, SFT-all, SM-DDPO, ReAct, and zero-shot LA-CDM. Backbone changes concern experimental configurations; the added cost controls are component ablations.

E3.justification: The default backbone changes from v1's inconsistently named Llama configuration to Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct. Reported training blocks increase from 50 to 100 steps per objective, and efficiency reporting changes from test counts to monetary costs. Appendix D adds retraining under altered cost schedules. The 80/10/10 split and existing preprocessing are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a cost-reward ablation and sensitivity analyses testing small price changes and an extreme CBC penalty. It removes v1 Appendix B's backbone/scale study, retains the hypothesis-agent ablation with updated settings, and replaces Figures 4–6 with different diagnostic trajectories, including repeated unsupported lipase requests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Both report predictive confidence and ECE; revised calibration values do not introduce a different statistical uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces most results: LA-CDM micro/macro F1 changes from 80.4/77.4 to 84.1/81.3, and SFT-all from 82.1/82.4 to 93.6/92.9. Changed models and training prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. Calibration results also change, including trained ECE from 0.150 to 0.037. Cost-ablation and sensitivity outcomes are added, while backbone results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds the mathematical definition of cumulative cost reward, R_cost(T) = -sum c(t), and Appendix C explains its normalization relative to the correct-diagnosis reward. Existing agent mappings and calibration mathematics remain; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the efficiency contribution from reducing diagnostic test counts to explicitly accounting for test prices and minimizing diagnostic cost. The central claims about trained, uncertainty-aware, hypothesis-driven clinical decision-making and patient-adaptive testing remain.

C2.justification: The discussion shifts from near-SFT-all performance with substantially fewer tests to monetary efficiency and accuracy tradeoffs. Appendix D interprets pricing robustness and the accuracy harm from avoiding informative CBC tests. v2 removes explicit four-disease, smaller-model, and prolonged-test-request limitations, while clarifying that optimization remains within clinician-demonstrated testing pathways.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access information, a reproducibility statement, charge tables and reward normalization, and clarification that history summarization excludes disease labels. It revises prompts and training/runtime details. v1's invalid-output scoring rules, calibration warm-up/exploration specifications, and asset-license appendix are no longer documented; these omissions alone do not establish execution changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Nori et al.'s sequential diagnosis work, Shao et al.'s DeepSeekMath/GRPO work, and Yang et al.'s Qwen report, while removing the Llama report citation. The related-work narrative and first-explicit-training novelty position remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 consolidates experimental/results subsection headings, moves preprocessing into Appendix C and societal-impact text into an ethics statement, revises prompts, and adds reproducibility and LLM-use statements. These are localized reorganizations rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different title, typography, and recurring-header layout, moves table captions above tables, and replaces test-count columns with cost columns. It adds cost and ablation tables, removes the backbone table, and substantially changes the case-study diagrams and their placement. Figures 1–2 retain their original schematics.

improvement.justification: v2 supports efficiency more directly through unequal test prices and a controlled ablation: Table 2 reports cost falling from $1427.85 to $1295.61 with micro F1 changing from 84.3 to 84.1. Pricing-sensitivity analyses and code-access documentation strengthen this contribution. Gains are limited by removed backbone evidence and scoring details, plus a reporting inconsistency: Table 3 shows higher cost with the hypothesis agent despite the retained claim of improvement in all metrics.
